segments.text: Two months ago, when I started my
Instagram channel, many of my friends
said, "Bro, the whole field is
saturated, there’s nothing left in
DSA, there are so many channels just
blabbering about studies." Anyway,
after one month, it has 300 followers
today. After that, when I started
YouTube, the same thing was said, "
Instagram allows anything, Instagram
followers have no value, YouTube won't
work, so many DSA channels have come
and gone, the field is fully saturated.
" Now, the YouTube channel has 11,000
followers too. So look, I never
believed in these things—that a field
is saturated, so you shouldn't pursue
it. There are already 15 people playing
cricket in the national team, so why
are the others working so hard? When
Sachin-ji was already playing, there
was no need for Kohli to do anything.
If Kohli is already playing, there
would have been no need for Shubman
Gill to do anything. So, it is
pointless to say that any field is
saturated. Someone might be telling you
that the job market is saturated. That
is not the case at all. No field is
ever saturated. There is a shortage of
talent in every field. If you are
better than the rest, you will find
your place. Someone will make space for
you. That was the first point. Now, as
this channel is slowly growing—it
reached 11,000 in one month. Two types
of things are happening now. The first
thing is that small YouTubers or
creators at my level, maybe someone has
5,000 or 15,000 followers. I mean,
those around my level, what are they
doing now? They are copying this,
basically starting to teach this DSA
pattern themselves. I don't have any
problem with this at all. Firstly, I
don't consider this copying. Because it
wasn't as if my idea was some unique
invention, like a medicine for a
disease that someone is copying. It was
just okay. DSA patterns weren't taught
that way before. I started teaching it.
Now some others have started teaching
it too. Copying won't change anything.
Copying doesn't bother me, nor does it
hurt them. If they have the strength
and the intelligence to copy this and
build a 1-million-subscriber channel in
a month, then by all means, do it. And
for anyone doing this, if you need any
help from my side, or if you feel we
should collaborate on something, please
DM me, message me, comment, whatever
you find convenient, do it anywhere.
And because I don't think you can
become better than someone by copying
them; a chef shares their recipe with
everyone, but it’s not like everyone
who follows that recipe starts making
food better than them, that doesn't
happen. So, that's all good, the more
it's being copied, the better it is, it
creates more of a wave. That’s one
thing I have no problem with, it's a
great thing, let it happen, let it be.
The second thing happening is that many
big YouTubers, those with 100k, 200k,
or even 1 million followers, what are
they doing now? They have started
criticizing this. There are many
LinkedIn posts claiming that if you
think reading 30 patterns will solve
your DSA problem-solving skills. If you
think you'll get a job, then we are
putting out a 1 lakh challenge. For
whom? For a mentor to come in front of
me. Solve any random LeetCode question
and take away ₹ 1 lakh. So first of
all, these kinds of posts and these
kinds of videos are logically very
foolish. Because look, for a random
LeetCode question, either you study
patterns, or you study DSA, or you
memorize 10,000 questions. No matter
what strategy you use to study DSA, you
can never guarantee that you will be
able to solve a random LeetCode
question. Why can't you? Because look,
a random LeetCode question is random,
isn't it, brother? What does a random
LeetCode question mean? It means it's
random. For example, if I start giving
random ones and click "Pick One."
That’s what random is, right? Now
look, this random question turned out
to be easy. This is an easy question.
So if I were in that challenge, I would
have solved this. I would have received
₹ 1 lakh. It’s possible that the
random question you pick could be hard
—so hard that no one could solve it
on the first try. So, I wouldn't get
the ₹ 1 lakh. So we can also put out
a similar challenge, that those who
teach DSA in such traditional ways, who
teach courses in traditional ways,
should come forward and solve a random
LeetCode problem in front of me; we
might not be able to offer 1 lakh.
Let's say, we can certainly offer
10,000. We will give you 10,000, and if
you can't solve it, you give us 1 lakh.
So, this challenge is open from my side
as well. Just like you threw the
challenge open. The same challenge is
open from my side too. You just say the
word. Whenever you want to do it, we
will do it, like that. Because this is
a very stupid way to prove your point;
this point is quite foolish. It's
illogical to say "solve a random
question to prove yourself." Why should
we solve a random question? There are
100,000 questions on LeetCode. No one
can solve every single question. Even
the person who wrote a book on the C
language cannot guarantee that they can
solve a random LeetCode question and
expect me to pay them 1 lakh rupees. So
, don't get caught up in these things.
This is just a way to fool people and
criticize them, nothing more. Now, the
real reason this criticism is happening
is their logic that studying patterns
—and look how their problem
statements and arguments will slowly
start to shift. Earlier, their argument
used to be, "Take my course.""You will
get a job." Everyone used to say, "My
course has 500 questions, 1,000
questions, whatever it is.""So take my
course.""You will get a job." Very good
. Now that people have started studying
patterns. Now that people have started
solving fewer questions by studying
patterns. Now their problem statement
is changing. Now they are saying, "Yes,
okay.""Studying patterns might get you
a job, but you won't gain
problem-solving skills.""How will you
become a good engineer, brother?""Your
DSA problem-solving skills won't be
good.""You might get a job.""I mean,
sure, you get a job.""Getting a job is
a good thing, but you won't learn
problem-solving." Look, the problem
here is that anyone can give long
speeches on philosophy or wisdom only
when their pockets are full. Right? You
don't do a job. You have such a big
YouTube channel. Such a huge social
media following. You are earning 1 lakh
rupees a month. You are sitting
comfortably at home in the AC after
having your meals. So if you are
sitting in the AC, you will think about
all these things. You will ponder this
philosophy of how to improve
problem-solving. Or how to get good
engineering done? So you, you can think
about all this. A kid who is in college
, who is in their third year, fourth
year, and has 2 days, 2 months, or 3
months left before placements. They
cannot think about all this philosophy
that I should first learn all of
problem-solving by spending 4 years and
only then apply for a job. When there
is no money in your pocket and no food
to eat. When parents scold you every
day that you haven't landed a job. At
that time, one doesn't think about the
philosophy of learning problem-solving
first. I am also saying the same thing.
See, what is the ideal way to study?
The ideal way, according to me as well,
I accept it. What is the ideal way to
study DSA according to me? You should
start from the very beginning of B.Tech
. In the first year, you should study
the basics of the language. In the
second and third year, you should
practice problems intensely to improve
your problem-solving. In the fourth
year, you should revise. This is the
ideal. But if you have reached the
fourth year. You have reached the third
year. You couldn't do anything in
college, just like I couldn't do
anything. So what will you do? Will you
find a technique to get a job
immediately, or will you think that no,
the ideal way is the 4-year one, so now
I will stay home for 4 years to prepare
and become a good engineer? Then you
won't get a job. Why? There will be a
gap in your resume. You will be asked
what you were doing for 4 years. You
will say I was becoming a good engineer
for 4 years. Then you will be told to
start your own company and become an
engineer there. Don't come to our
company. So all these philosophies and
good talks are for those whose basic
problems are already solved. Solve your
basic problems first. Food, drink,
shelter, clothing—get all these
sorted out. After that, you can dive
into philosophy—that now I will do
this, I will do that, I will build
castles in the air, this and that. So,
all this philosophy suits only rich
people. There was a dialogue by Shah
Rukh Khan that first become rich, then
become a philosopher. Gautam Buddha was
a king, only then did he become Gautam
Buddha. If you ask a beggar in Bodh
Gaya what the truth of life is...Then
he will say that the truth of life is
bread. It doesn't matter to me what the
truth or the lie is. Right? So, do not
get involved in all this. The reason
for the criticism is that their courses
are running. Some have a 6-month course
, some have a 2-year course, some have
a 2. 1/2-year course. Someone is doing
500 questions. Someone is doing 1200
questions. Someone is even doing 2000.
Now they feel that a shift is coming
from this. A revolution is coming.
Slowly, the wave is changing. And they
feel that if they don't stop it right
now, this wave will keep growing. So, I
have no request for them, nothing at
all. I mean, I am a very small person.
I cannot say anything to you. And that
is why I will not use any images on
thumbnails either, because I feel
worried about when someone might file a
strike or copyright claim, so I won't
do that, nor will I take any names. So,
I have one request for you, that it's
fine, criticize as much as you want
right now. Whenever something good
comes into the market, people criticize
it. In 2014-15, when online education
first came, people said, "Oh, online
education is nothing." They are all
jokers. Right? These people don't know
how to teach. Those who ran offline
centers used to say, "Oh, all these
online guys are jokers." What will
these people teach? Is studies even
possible online? Will studies happen by
sitting in a center room, or will they
happen online on a laptop? Now just
look. Each person who came into online
education at that time. That one
person's net worth has become more than
the net worth of that entire center.
Just that joker, whom people used to
call a joker. So these things are good.
Both things are good. Whenever you feel
that you are doing something that is
being copied and about which bad things
are also being said, then you are doing
something different. If you have no
enemies, it means you are not doing
anything. Meaning, someone who has no
enemies and no criticism is not doing
anything in the world. They are just
going along with the crowd, thinking, "
Yes, it's fine, I'll live like this or
like that." So, I really like both
things. I welcome both with an open
heart. Yes, I have one request for all
those who are currently saying, "What
is the point of studying patterns?"
Please don't go and launch your own
courses after two or three months.
Right? Listen to this carefully. You
guys should talk now. You should say
now, "Yes, what is the point of
studying patterns?" But two months
later, when this becomes famous, when
it becomes even more popular. 6 months
later, when this entire wave changes
the way DSA is studied. At that time,
there shouldn't be any "A to Z Patterns
" or "Complete Patterns in One Shot" or
any "Strike,""Aakraman,""Arjun," or "
Bheem" batch from you. Right? Don't
launch it, because that would be
hypocrisy, wouldn't it? You are saying
right now that studying this is useless
. You say you won't learn good problem
solving from this. You won't be able to
learn engineering. Then after 4 months,
you will go and launch a batch saying,
"Come on guys, join our pattern batch."
"We teach using patterns in this one."
So please don't do that. If you do that
at that time, we will make another
video to remind you. So that is my one
request; otherwise, keep doing whatever
you want to do. It's your channel; you
have freedom of expression. Speak up,
speak as much as you want. Uh, keep
posting as much as you want. Keep
putting up your ₹ 1 lakh, ₹ 2 lakh,
₹ 1 lakh challenges. Whenever I need
money, if there's ever a time I need
money, I will definitely think about
your challenge, thinking if I can get
₹ 1 lakh just by solving a random
question. So now look, I opened this
right in front of you, didn't I? This
is on video, there are no edits here. I
went here, clicked 'Pick One', and this
opened up. For those who are throwing
out challenges, if I solve this
question right now? Then will you give
me ₹ 20,000, if not ₹ 1 lakh?
20,000 would at least get some work
done for me; I'll buy something with
that 20,000. So, if I solve this
question, then give me 20,000. If you
think that's fair, then say so, and I
will solve this question next time.
Right? And I will make a video like
that too. I'll open a random question
and solve it. If I solve it, you give
me 20,000. Brother, you have plenty of
money anyway. Okay? And the same
challenge is from my side as well. I
can't give 1 lakh. I will give 10,000.
Right? So you can also solve a LeetCode
problem. So that’s it, and the study
video will likely come out in the
evening. Because on Saturday...look,
you guys don't study much on Saturdays
and Sundays, I can tell that from the
trends. That’s why making these
videos is also necessary, because when
something is being made, people write
in the comments that 'Hey, this is
being copied,' some say this, some say
that. People are tagging me on LinkedIn
, saying 'Hey, look at this, you were
saying this, they are saying that.' So,
it’s important for me to respond too,
so you don't feel like Pratyush Bhaiya
is fooling you. Because people think
that the one who isn't speaking up must
be in the wrong. Someone is out there
giving big speeches, saying 'Oh, this
is wrong, he is a thief.' And you start
thinking that since this person isn't
saying anything......he must really be
a thief. He must really be fooling
people. So, these things are necessary.
You have to understand what is logical,
like 'I'll give you 1 lakh rupees, I'll
do this, I'll do that.' Nobody wants
anyone else's 1 lakh rupees. Many
people can make up a lot of stories
like that. Even someone who doesn't
have 10,000 rupees can claim they will
give away 1 crore. Such things have
happened before. They will keep
happening in the future. There’s no
need to stress about it. At least, I
don't. And I am telling the students
the same thing: don’t stress. A new
revolution in learning is coming. The
way DSA was taught and the way it was
learned, both are slowly changing.
Right? People who are already settled
are afraid of change. Offline centers
were very afraid of coming online
because they thought things would
change. In the same way, those who are
currently settled are afraid that
things will change and they will become
obsolete. But that is the rule. Right
now, I am doing something. A year from
now, if God is kind and I grow a bit,
someone else will come and change this.
They will say 'this is wrong and this
is right,' and that will become the new
standard. So, I will also have to shift
accordingly. I can't just say, 'Oh no,
he's crazy, he's talking nonsense, he's
a thief.''He is just fooling people.'
We cannot say that. Change is the only
constant in the world. Right? So, this
was a short video from my side, and my
purpose for LeetCode was just that, you
know about random questions? What is it
? A random question. Random means
random, brother. On LeetCode, there's
easy, medium, and hard. There are
questions you can solve in a single
line. And in hard, there are questions
that even if we spend a day, we won't
be able to solve. No matter how many
patterns I teach, or how well I explain
algorithms and keep giving speeches. I
won't be able to do it in a day. I
admit that, and neither will you.
It’s possible there’s a question
that even you might not be able to
solve. So, LeetCode random is nothing.
Random means random. Let’s meet later
. Right?
